description.value: This study investigated whether phenocopy frontotemporal dementia belongs to the same disease spectrum as behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia by comparing default mode network connectivity and white matter microstructural measures between groups.

spans.text: This study investigates whether phFTD patients have underlying brain abnormalities that are similar to those seen in bvFTD patients: functional brain abnormalities expressed as DMN connectivity changes and microstructural WM abnormalities expressed as diffusion changes.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison of phenocopy frontotemporal dementia patients, behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia patients and healthy controls.

spans.text: Seven phFTD patients without progression or alternative psychiatric diagnosis, 12 bvFTD patients and 17 controls underwent resting state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI).

description.value: Seven phenocopy frontotemporal dementia (phFTD) patients with prominent behavioural changes, no disease progression, and no alternative psychiatric diagnosis; studied for functional connectivity and white-matter microstructural abnormalities.

spans.text: PhFTD patients (aged 40-75 years) with prominent behavioural changes interfering with social functioning, consisting of disinhibition and/or apathy and/or stereotypy; no reported progression 1 year after initial routine diagnostic workup, and bvFTD patients (aged 45-70 years) with a diagnosis of bvFTD [ 17 ]; a clinical dementia rating scale score of ≤1; and a Mini-Mental State Examination [ 18 ] (MMSE) score of ≥ 20 were included in the study.
